verdict.rationale: dlt ships an official MCP server (dlt-mcp) exposing tools for inspecting/debugging/managing pipelines, plus a dedicated 'AI Harness' of skills, rules, and MCP servers explicitly designed to let general-purpose coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) build, deploy, and operate pipelines from natural-language requests (e.g. 'I want to ingest pull requests and issues from the GitHub REST API'), and markets itself as 'Built for LLMs with 8000+ source connectors.' This directly supports AI-native users issuing natural-language commands to build/operate pipelines, though it operates through an external coding-agent layer rather than dlt parsing NL itself. Missing for 10: independent/hands-on evidence of the AI Harness actually succeeding on real NL requests, and detail on the breadth/limits of natural-language commands it reliably supports.
